harness.caller: runtime.cli_v1.mcp_server.create_server over guarded-x11 public MCP tools
harness.supervisor_target: wrapper starts a real separate bystander client and invokes unchanged x11_cancel_worker

environment.preflight: No /tmp/.X178-lock or /tmp/.X11-unix/X178; no exact Xvfb :178 process observed

procedure: Start exactly one private Xvfb :178 at 800x600x24 with TCP disabled.
Create a synthetic target window, observe and mint through standard public MCP tools, then admit one synthetic key action.
Use the existing integration owner factory to queue the delayed XTEST event and block its real python-xlib Display.sync call.
Invoke public interface_guarded_cancel and allow normal owner retirement and prestarted supervisor dispatch.
Inside the test-only supervisor wrapper, start one distinct process whose first X connection is the post-retirement bystander; record its PID and resource base.
If the bystander naturally reused the retired owner's exact XRes base, call unchanged x11_cancel_worker while that client remains connected; otherwise record HOLD and do not run cleanup worker.

Require the public terminal result to remain UNKNOWN/no-replay, worker to report resource_base_reused_by_unrelated_client and not_attempted, and independent keymap readback to retain the key-down state before harness cleanup.
Release isolated synthetic keys, wait through the declared delayed-request horizon, verify final neutral state, stop the exact private Xvfb, and preserve all raw files.

one_shot.if_resource_base_not_reused: HOLD; worker not invoked; no XID forcing or rerun

claim_boundary: One public-caller live-Xvfb bystander-refusal sample only. No physical desktop/MAP01, global input exclusivity, task-success, hard OS bound, matched efficiency/reliability, or WSLc portability claim.
